claims.claim: For a German student visa applied for in India, an APS certificate is always mandatory unless an exception applies.
An APS certificate is not needed if you will obtain a non-German degree in Germany.
An APS certificate is not needed if you will do PhD/postdoc studies.
An APS certificate is not needed if you received a scholarship from German or EU public funds.
An APS certificate is not needed if your studies build on a non-Indian school certificate (e.g. International Baccalaureate) or a non-Indian degree (e.g. a British Bachelor).
APS-requiring bachelor/master applicants, scholarship holders and PhD/postdoc applicants go to VFS.
Those studying for non-German degrees apply at the Embassy or a Consulate.
Booking an appointment in the wrong category means the application won't be accepted.
Universities may set their own APS rules.
Applicants with an Indian school or university degree must have their certificates checked by APS in New Delhi (per TUM).
The checklist is dated September 2024.

reference_key_facts: APS certificate is mandatory for Indian applicants for a German student visa
Exception: obtaining a non-German degree in Germany
correctness.explanation: The assistant says an APS certificate is generally mandatory unless an exception applies. It lists the non-German degree, PhD/postdoc and scholarship exceptions, so every key fact is covered. The extra details, such as the non-Indian school certificate exception and the VFS/Embassy distinction, do not contradict the reference.

claims.claim: Most international students use a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of sufficient funds, with the money shown as a credit to the account.
A Sperrkonto may only allow a certain level of withdrawals each month.
A Sperrkonto can only be closed with approval from an embassy, consulate or the competent foreigners authority.
The German embassy in India currently requires €11,904 for the first year of studies in a blocked account.
No more than €992 per month can be withdrawn from the blocked account.
An alternative to a blocked account is a formal obligation letter (Verpflichtungserklärung) from a sponsor living in Germany.
An alternative to a blocked account is proof of a German/EU scholarship or stipend.
Sperrkonten are available from several providers.
The best approach is to get advice from the German embassy or consulate.

reference_key_facts: Most international students use a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of funds
correctness.explanation: The assistant says most international students use a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of sufficient funds, which matches the reference's key fact. The extra details about withdrawal limits, alternatives and amounts do not contradict it.
